direct_answer: No. Aker BP states that it “does not have a climate transition plan in line with the ESRS' requirements” and that it “do[es] not have a timeline for if or when [it] will develop such a plan,” citing the absence of scope 3 emissions reduction targets as the reason. [Source 1]
compliance_rationale: ESRS E1-1 requires disclosure of a climate change mitigation transition plan, or if none exists, whether and when it will be adopted. Aker BP explicitly discloses that it does not have an ESRS-aligned climate transition plan and provides no timeline to develop one. [Source 1]
disclosure_gaps: No ESRS E1-1 transition plan disclosed (e.g., 1.5°C compatibility, decarbonisation levers/actions across own operations and value chain, investments/funding, locked-in emissions assessment, taxonomy alignment objectives, governance approval, and progress). [Source 1]
No indication of whether it will adopt an ESRS-aligned transition plan and, if so, by when (company states it has no timeline). [Source 1]
key_findings: Aker BP reports it has no scope 3 emissions reduction targets. [Source 1]
Aker BP concludes it therefore does not have a climate transition plan in line with ESRS requirements. [Source 1]
Aker BP reports it has no timeline for developing such a plan. [Source 1]
